video.scriptStarter: Listen to the guide's account: A Motion asks the court to act, a Brief presents legal arguments, and a Deposition records testimony outside trial under the required procedure. reading.title: The Courtroom: A practical discussion
reading.text: In a civil example, the Plaintiff brings a claim against the Defendant. A Jury may consider Evidence where the procedure provides for one. The presence of a claim does not establish that it is correct. A Document may provide recorded information. An Oath commits a witness to truthfulness, and a Verdict records the specified decision. Cross-Examine describes questioning the opposing witness under the procedure. Before reaching a decision, the jurors Deliberate by considering and discussing the evidence under the court’s instructions. The account describes decision-making vocabulary without predicting a result.
reading.imageBrief: One uncluttered courtroom setting supporting this written account. Show only details actually described, without invented procedures, readable text or implied official approval. The text supplies facts that cannot be seen.
